title-proc.eng: The collection, transportation and treatment of bio waste.

description-proc.eng: The Contracting Authority Avfall Sør Husholdning AS is a part of Avfall Sør konsern, which is owned 100% by Kristiansand and Vennesla municipalities in Agder. The company provides waste and sanitation services to all inhabitants in the owner municipalities and serves approx. 55,500 residential units with dunk sanitation, 5,000 residential units with buried systems and 3,700 cabin subscribers. In addition, the company operates three recycling stations and a large waste facility at Støleheia with various treatment activities such as sorting, composting, tiling and depositing. Avfall Sør Husholdning AS is the contracting authority for this competition. Read more about Avfall Sør at: www.avfallsor.no Background Avfall Sør Husholdning AS is currently collecting food and bio waste from households in the owner municipalities. The waste is transported to Støleheia, where it is composted in a separate facility. The finished compost is to be refined to soil products that are traded for various purpose. From 1 September the new supplier will take over the collection of household waste on behalf of the contracting authority. The collection routes are thus altered and the collection frequency for food and bio-waste is changed from weekly to collection every two weeks. The change is a part of Avfall Sør ́s work with increasing the sorting of food and bio waste. Analyses show that there are still significant amounts of food waste in the residue waste, and the aim is to move a greater share of this to the bio-waste scheme. At the same time, garden and park waste makes up a significant part of the total amount of bio-waste. In 2025, this fraction accounted for about 20 percent of the total tonnage. Avfall Sør also handles municipal commercial waste on behalf of the owner municipalities. This waste flow is mainly equivalent to composition and quality as bio-waste from households, but normally contains a lower portion of garden and park waste. The new manure products regulation, which came into force in 2025, sets strict requirements for businesses that produce natural fertiliser products of organic origin. Amongst other things, the requirements for quality assurance, documentation, traceability, internal control and product responsibility have been strengthened. Fulfilment of these requirements would require considerable investments in infrastructure, process installations, quality systems and further development of the composting facility. After a combined assessment of investment needs, operational finances, regulation requirements and future treatment systems, Avfall Sør Husholdning AS has therefore decided to discontinue separate composting of bio waste. Instead, the collection, transport and treatment of the bio-waste will be outsourced so that the waste can be treated at an external facility with the necessary capacity and competence to meet the current requirements. This solution is considered the most cost efficient and robust in the long term, while ensuring that bio-waste is treated in accordance with current regulations and can be utilised as a valuable circular resource. Description of the assignment The contracting authority needs a robust and environmentally responsible system for handling bio-waste (food and garden/park), from households and business customers. The procurement shall ensure continuity in the receipt, transport and treatment of waste, and contribute to the waste being used as a resource through material recovery and/or energy recovery. The aim of the procurement is to establish a contract with a tenderer who can safeguard the entire value chain from collection at the contracting authority ́s waste facility at Støleheia, until final treatment. The system shall support the contracting authority ́s work on sustainable waste management in the region around Kristiansand and contribute to predictable operation in the contract period. The procurement is particularly important in order to ensure sufficient treatment capacity, stable logistics and a system that fulfils the current environmental requirements as well as requirements for proper handling of the bio waste. The contracting authority may also receive and process bio-waste from both households and commercial customers on behalf of other municipalities in the region around us. These volumes will then be able to flow to this contract and are taken into consideration in the competition ́s value limitations. The contract will be valid for 1 year, with an option for the contracting authority to extend the contract for 1 year at a time for up to 3 years, so that the maximum total contract period is 4 years.

title-proc.eng: Dublin City Council Contract for Architect Led Integrated Design Team for the Installation of a Pontoon at Islandbridge

description-proc.eng: The stretch of the River Liffey near Islandbridge, is home to over 13 Rowing Clubs – one of which belongs to Dublin City Council. In order to link the eastern length of the Liffey from Islandbridge, the Community, Culture and Local Area Services Department of Dublin City Council has obtained planning permission for an access walkway and pontoon to be constructed on one of the small islands east of the weir. This will allow rowers starting at Islandbridge to have access down to Ringsend and vice versa safely. The project comprises a pontoon with associated walkways to facilitate access to the river for rowing boats and kayaks. The project will provide for a platform that would minimize damage to bankside vegetation when launching and retrieving boats and allow a safe platform for kayakers and boaters to embark and disembark. The Islandbridge location has extensive heritage and ecology. In keeping with this, minimal deviation from the existing design and methodology is required to comply with planning regulations. The works proposed plan to combine the following elements: a) A floating pontoon system within the River Liffey anchored to the existing island shore. b) A new stone and concrete platform built out from the riverbank and connected to the pontoon by a new gangway. c) The removal of vegetation on approach to the pontoon and installation of a new access walkway from the south upper River Liffey at the weir to the new pontoon located north on the lower River Liffey. d) The temporary removal, refurbishment and reinstatement of an existing steel footbridge located on the island. e) The removal of poor existing vegetation, pruning of existing healthy trees and the replanting of 25 new high-quality trees and growing shrubs all native to Ireland. f) Temporary regrading of land during site works for access onto the island. . The current system in the lab is running on Empower and hence the new system must be able to upgrade from an older Empower license. • The nanoflow system must be able to do both nanoflow and microflow on the same device capable of delivering flow rates between 200 nL/min to 100 uL/min. title-proc.eng: Satellite Orthoimages in Finland 2027

description-proc.eng: GENERAL Please note that this is a prior information notice (hereafter “notice”) and not a call for tenders. The information provided in this notice is preliminary and may change during the preparation phase. Hansel Oy acts in a consultative role in this procurement. DESCRIPTION OF THE PROCUREMENT National Land Survey of Finland ("NLS") is planning to purchase satellite orthoimages covering areas in Finland. The production areas to be ordered are based on the national aerial imaging programme, under which Finland will be aerially imaged over a period of three years, excluding the northernmost parts of Lapland. The upcoming procurement forms part of the NLS' preparedness for the situation where aerial images cannot be obtained from all production areas due to GNSS interference. The acquisition time for the satellite orthoimages is approximately from April to August. The satellite orthoimages must be snow free with minimum cloud coverage. The maximum resolution of the orthoimage is 0.5 m. Satellite orthoimages must be mosaicked seamlessly and delivered as 6*6 km grids that are fully covered, with minimum four bands (Red (R), Green (G), Blue (B) and Near InfraRed (Nir). The orthoimages must be delivered fully processed including radiometric correction, georectification, orthorectification and atmospheric compensation (i.e., GIS ready images) following the requirements listed in the final call for tenders. The upcoming procurement is planned to cover the possible needs for satellite orthoimages for year 2027. REGISTRATION Companies interested in this upcoming procurement are requested to submit their contact details by email to kilpailutus@hansel.fi. Please use the subject line: “NLS: Satellite Orthomosaics in Finland”. MARKET DIALOGUE Companies that register by 30th October 2026 will be given the opportunity to comment on the draft materials during the commenting period (approximately 2nd November - 6th November). Registered companies will be able to provide written comments on the draft materials. NLS reserves the possibility for additional commenting rounds and/or meetings or phone calls if deemed necessary for the preparation of the procurement. Participation or non‑participation in the market dialogue does not affect eligibility to participate in the tender procedure.

title-proc.eng: Market Dialogue: City Bike Procurement (Lahti / Kuopio)

description-proc.eng: The cities of Lahti and Kuopio are preparing a possible future procurement of bike-sharing services. As part of the procurement preparation process, we invite potential service providers to participate in a market dialogue. The purpose of the market dialogue is to gain insight into available solutions and market capabilities, discuss the contracting authorities' objectives and requirements, and gather feedback to support the development of a practical, transparent, and competitive procurement process. This market consultation is intended to gather information and feedback from potential service providers to support the preparation of a possible future procurement. Participation is voluntary, does not create any obligations for either party, and is neither a prerequisite or an advantage in any future tender process. The contracting authorities are not obliged to proceed with the procurement or to take into account any views expressed during the consultation. No compensation will be paid for participation and all information provided will be used solely for procurement preparation purposes. BACKGROUND The cities of both Lahti and Kuopio currently operate public bike-sharing systems and are preparing for the next contract periods. Lahti and Kuopio are regional cities of comparable size and have experience in operating similar electrically assisted bike-sharing systems. This provides an opportunity to explore the possibility of joint procurement while enabling the contracting authorities to benefit from shared experience, common requirements, and potential economies of scale. The aim of both cities is to procure a flexible, reliable, and userfriendly bike-sharing service, with the possibility of including the surrounding municipalities of both city regions. After registration, participants will receive a Microsoft Teams invitation, meeting agenda and preliminary questions, which we kindly ask them to review before the meeting. For tenderers’ information, a low-complexity spine patient is defined as an individual with a straightforward, one or two level or localised spinal condition that requires standard surgical or medical management with minimal technical difficulty and lower physiological risk. title-proc.eng: Loppa municipality - Molo - Øksfjord Harbour

description-proc.eng: On behalf of Loppa municipality, tenderers are invited to a competition for improvements to the port conditions in Øksfjord. The General contract (NS 8406) includes the establishment of two new piers, the establishment of a new pumping station, a sewage pipeline and an access road. Dredging the seabed under Molo South is necessary to ensure sufficient geotechnical stability before completion. Dredging masses shall be reused as core masses in the piers and for filling ditches, while any surplus matter is delivered to an approved site. The work shall be carried out with environmental measures such as bubble curtain and turbidity monitoring. The existing sewage pipeline must have been moved and relaid with a new pumping station before sea work starts. The pier North shall be partially established before dredging starts to enable encapsulation of the dredging masses and reduce particle dispersion. The contract includes further filling work, width expansion and extension of Pier North, establishment of a turnaround, as well as concrete work on a new and existing pier. The concrete works are options and include casting breakwater covers, parapets and casting on existing constructions. The builder is free to order all or parts of the optioned concrete works. The execution shall be carried out in accordance with the engineering design documentation and the accompanying drawings. Furthermore, there are option posts for the demolition and re-establishment of approx. 200 metres of existing sewage pipeline on land.

Additional Services may be procured through the course of the framework to facilitate various investigative activities including but not limited to the following areas of work:- • Process Optimisation • Process Proving / Commissioning These additional services may be PLANNED or UNPLANNED in nature. Lot 2: Provision of Wastewater Laboratory Testing Services. Uisce Eireann require wastewater laboratory testing services for the following sampling categories: • PLANNED (Wastewater Regulatory Sampling Plans ) • UNPLANNED (Investigative; Short term requests e.g. EPA) • EMERGENCY. With regards to the PLANNED, UNPLANNED, and EMERGENCY categories, Uisce Eireann may also require sampling and/or testing of In-Process Wastewater (i.e. samples taken from locations within the treatment process). Off-grid solutions can power over 400 million people across Africa and LAC. Off- Grid Regulation and Market Development establishes a framework for public partners to strengthen institutional capacities to accomplish their rural development mandates, as well as market incentives that promote private sector participation and finance for scaling projects. ? In addition to its core activities, GET.transform has implemented TA services to other GIZ- programs in Africa, Latin America and the Caribbean, as well as Asia and Europe. description-proc.fra: Prestations de services relatives à l’exploitation et à la maintenance (O&M) du parc éolien de Saint-Vith, comprenant cinq machines Vestas V90-2.0 MW Mk7 pour une puissance installée totale de 10 MW. Les prestations comprennent notamment la maintenance préventive, corrective, le dépannage, la surveillance à distance 24h/24 et 7j/7, la gestion des pièces de rechange et l'intégration des données opérationnelles de monitoring.
description-proc.eng: Provision of operation and maintenance (O&M) services for the 5 wind turbines (Vestas V90-2.0 MW Mk7, total capacity 10 MW) of the Saint-Vith wind farm, including preventive and corrective maintenance, 24/7 remote monitoring, spare parts management, and monitoring data integration.

title-proc.eng: Framework agreement - Purchase of fittings for glass insulator strings - 26/17723

description-proc.eng: The Contracting Authority wants to purchase complete glass insulator strings. For further details regarding the purchase, reference is made to the tender documents: Ap-pendix 2A scope of works for powerlines and 2B Scope of work for substations. The tendered framework agreement has a duration of four (4) years. The framework agree-ment can be extended two (2) times for two (2) years each time. The framework agreement is divided into the following lots: • Lot 1: Complete glass insulator strings for powerlines. Expected consumption to be: EUR 10.000.000. Maximum value is EUR 24.000.000 • Lot 2: Complete glass insulator strings for substations. Expected consumption to be: EUR: 2.684.563,75. Maximum value is EUR 6.442.953,00 euro. Tenders can be submitted for all Lots. Tenderers are not required to submit a tender for both lots Offers can be submitted for all partial agreements The estimated consumption during the term of the framework agreement is expected to amount to be divided into lots. The consumption figures are estimates only and are consequently not binding for the Contract-ing Authority. During the specified period, the Contracting Authority has the right to purchase the services and/or goods comprised by the framework agreement from the selected tenderer but is not obligated to do so cf. the framework sec. 1.3.
